# Flying Mink Drone Solutions (פליינג מינק)

> Israeli drone services and drone education business operating across Israel, with most instructors in the Center and Sharon regions. Founded and run by Maor Shtolz, a commercial-licensed drone operator with an operational background as a drone operator in an elite IDF unit. The site is in Hebrew and offers a free online drone course, a "which drone should I buy" quiz, drone laws by country, an interactive Israeli flight-zone map, drone workshops for schools, private flying lessons and aerial photography.

Contact: WhatsApp +972-54-990-2676 · maorshtolz@gmail.com · Instagram @flyingmink · https://flyingmink.com

## Services

- [Drone workshops for schools](https://flyingmink.com/schools.html): workshops for elementary schools, middle schools, high schools and pre-military academies (מכינות קדם-צבאיות), from a single session up to a five-session program; also peak days (ימי שיא) and drone activities for groups of all ages. Students learn how drones fly, fly themselves under instructor supervision, and learn aerial photography, FPV and safety.
- [Private drone flying lessons](https://flyingmink.com/program.html): one-on-one 1.5-hour lesson for one person in the Sharon flight bubble (בועת השרון), on Flying Mink's drone, 500 ILS. Includes an intro flight and safe-flying and beginner photography basics, a one-on-one training presentation, key drone laws and tips, access to recorded videos, and access to lessons that help with the Israeli commercial drone license theory exam. No FPV lessons.
- [Aerial photography](https://flyingmink.com/photography.html): drone photography for weddings, events, sports events, municipal events, real estate, construction and marketing content.

## Key facts — flying a drone in Israel

- Since November 2024 everyone who flies a drone in Israel needs a license: a recreational license (רישיון מטיסן) for leisure, or a small-UAS pilot license (רישיון מטיס כטב"ם קטן) for any commercial flying. This applies to drones under 250 g too.
- The recreational license is an online test through the Civil Aviation Authority system: 15 questions, 12 correct answers to pass. Available from age 12; children under 12 fly only under close supervision of a licensed person aged 16+.
- Drones over 250 g must be registered for recreational flying; for commercial operation every drone is registered.
- Maximum height 50 m above ground unless the AIP (פמ"ת) says otherwise; keep within 500 m and direct line of sight.
- No flying in prohibited, restricted or dangerous zones published in the AIP or NOTAMs, near airfields, or within set distances of military sites. Check the official sport-aviation map before each flight.

Details and sources: https://flyingmink.com/faq.html
